body_markdown:
Alcohol addiction can gradually take over a person's health, relationships, finances and sense of hope. For Toby Winson, the consequences of alcohol dependence became impossible to ignore when he was just 25. After years of heavy drinking, he developed alcoholic liver disease and noticed that the whites of his eyes had turned yellow, a symptom associated with jaundice.


Today, Toby is approaching 10 years sober and has built a very different life. His story highlights the seriousness of alcohol dependence, the dangers of withdrawal, and the importance of asking for help.


## How Toby's Alcohol Addiction Began


According to a report published by the *Mirror* , Toby began drinking vodka with friends when he was 14. By the age of 19, drinking had become a private daily routine. He would often drink alone and hide the extent of his alcohol use from those around him.


Over time, alcohol became more than something he enjoyed. It became something he felt he needed.


Toby described addiction as taking control of his life. He continued drinking despite warning signs and eventually found himself physically dependent on alcohol.


This progression is important because alcohol dependence does not always appear suddenly. Drinking can become increasingly frequent and difficult to control, while a person may continue hiding the problem from family and friends.


## Yellow Eyes Became a Major Warning Sign


At the height of his addiction, Toby's drinking reached extremely dangerous levels. The report says he was consuming around one and a half litres of vodka during one period before switching to large quantities of strong white cider because it was cheaper.


Eventually, he noticed that the whites of his eyes had become yellow.


The change frightened him. He went to hospital and was diagnosed with alcoholic liver disease. He reportedly spent a month in hospital while doctors worked to save his life.


Yellowing of the skin or whites of the eyes can be a sign of jaundice and should not be ignored. There can be many possible causes, including serious liver problems, so anyone experiencing unexplained yellowing should seek medical attention.


Toby's experience demonstrates how severe alcohol-related health problems can become, particularly when heavy drinking continues for years.


## The Hidden Dangers of Alcohol Withdrawal


One of the most serious aspects of Toby's story was what happened when he suddenly stopped drinking.


After years of heavy alcohol use, he experienced severe withdrawal symptoms, including vomiting, hallucinations and seizures. He described seeing things that were not actually there and becoming extremely confused and frightened.


Doctors later warned him that suddenly stopping alcohol could be dangerous because his body had become physically dependent on it.


This is an important lesson for anyone experiencing alcohol dependence. Stopping alcohol suddenly after prolonged heavy drinking can carry serious medical risks. People who believe they may be physically dependent should seek professional medical advice rather than attempting to manage severe withdrawal alone.


Treatment may involve medical supervision, structured detoxification and ongoing support.


## When Addiction Affects the Whole Family


Toby's addiction did not only affect his own health. It also placed enormous emotional pressure on his family.


For years, he concealed how much he was drinking. He described carrying toothpaste to disguise the smell of alcohol and hiding empty bottles.


Eventually, his family discovered the severity of the situation.


At one point, his mother was placed in the distressing position of rationing vodka while Toby waited for a place at a detoxification centre because doctors believed abruptly stopping could put his life at risk.


This illustrates how addiction can affect everyone around the person struggling with it. Families can experience fear, confusion, guilt and helplessness while trying to support someone they love.


## Reaching Rock Bottom


By the age of 24, Toby was unemployed and living alone. His life had become centred around obtaining enough alcohol to prevent withdrawal symptoms.


He reportedly moved from vodka to inexpensive, high-strength cider because it was more affordable. During particularly difficult periods, he struggled to find money for alcohol and even sold possessions.


His daily routine became extremely destructive. He described waking with severe stomach pain, making himself sick and then drinking to manage withdrawal symptoms.


The situation eventually became even more dangerous when, during a relapse, he drank hand sanitiser in a hospital toilet and was admitted to intensive care.


For Toby, August 2016 became the turning point. It was the month he had his final drink.


## Recovery Started With Honesty


Toby says one of the most important parts of his recovery was learning to speak openly about his addiction.


Instead of hiding what had happened, he began talking honestly about his experiences. He also introduced healthier routines and started setting small goals.


Those goals did not initially have to be dramatic. Something as simple as walking his dog helped him reconnect with everyday life.


This is a valuable reminder that recovery does not necessarily happen through one enormous transformation. Progress can involve many small, consistent steps.


Over time, Toby says the shame and guilt he experienced began to fade. Pride gradually replaced some of the negative feelings associated with his past.


## Building a New Life After Addiction


Toby's life today looks very different from the years when alcohol controlled him.


He has become an award-winning journalist and recovery advocate. He has also presented documentaries about alcohol-related harm and spoken to young people about addiction.


He says that openly discussing his recovery has remained an important part of staying sober.


His experience also taught him that addiction can take different forms. After overcoming alcohol dependence, he later struggled with gambling. He recognised that keeping the problem hidden made it harder to address.


As a result, he adopted the same principle of openness and accountability that had helped him with alcohol recovery.


## Recovery Can Be Possible


Perhaps the most hopeful part of Toby's story is what happened after his darkest period.


According to the *Mirror* , scans showed that his liver had healed and that he had avoided permanent cirrhosis. He also rebuilt his relationship with his family and developed a career centred partly around helping others understand addiction.


His story does not suggest that recovery is easy. Instead, it shows that a person can move from severe addiction towards a healthier and more meaningful life with appropriate support.


For people struggling with alcohol addiction, reaching out can be an important first step. Support may come through a GP, local alcohol services, counselling, mutual-support organisations or trusted people in their lives.


Most importantly, someone experiencing addiction does not have to face it in silence.


## Final Thoughts


Toby Winson's experience is a powerful example of how alcohol addiction can affect physical health, mental wellbeing, relationships and everyday life. His diagnosis of alcoholic liver disease at 25 showed the potentially devastating consequences of long-term heavy drinking.


Yet his story also demonstrates that a serious addiction does not necessarily have to define the rest of a person's life.


Recovery can begin with honesty, professional support and small achievable goals. For someone trapped in addiction, the future may feel impossible to imagine. Toby's journey offers a different message: change can happen, and asking for help can be the beginning of that change.
